title: Universal Jurisdiction and Accountability for Atrocity Crimes
seo_title: Universal Jurisdiction and Accountability for Atrocity Crimes
excerpt: Universal jurisdiction allows national courts to investigate and prosecute grave international crimes even when the alleged conduct occurred abroad, involved foreign perpetrators and victims, and lacks an ordinary territorial connection to the forum state. This article explains how universal jurisdiction operates as a decentralized accountability tool for atrocity crimes, including genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, torture, enforced disappearance, and related international crimes. It examines treaty duties, customary international law, aut dedere aut judicare, complementarity, immunity, extradition, asylum, evidence-sharing, witness protection, digital documentation, civil-society case files, and strategic litigation. The article also addresses selectivity, political backlash, forum shopping, due process, and the relationship between domestic courts, the ICC, and international investigative mechanisms. By combining doctrine, case studies, and lawyer-facing workflows, it shows how universal jurisdiction can turn impunity gaps into concrete legal proceedings.
